Title: Ready... Set... Ignite!
NewsSubTitle: Promoting creativity and innovation at AKU
NewsSummary: CCIT's first effort was an Ignite event. Ignite is similar to TED Talks but with more stringent rules.
NewsContent:
Tunnel vision plagues the medical profession. One can see it in medical research, in clinical practice and in what is probably its saddest consequence, its future, i.e. medical students. One unintended consequence of all the knowledge that we have at our fingertips is that we have lost sight of the bigger picture, the part where all this information must come together to serve one purpose, to benefit the patient. Research is being done for the sake of doing research. Innovation and creativity are considered inferior to knowledge, not its equals.

A fledgling effort to combat this notion is the Critical, Creative and Innovative Thinking Forum (CCIT). A collaborative effort between Dr Asad I. Mian, a paediatric emergentologist and two fifth-year medical students, Faysal Subhani and Kanwal Nayani, this is a trans-generational, inter-disciplinary platform to promote out-of-the-box thinking.

CCIT's first effort was an Ignite event. Ignite is similar to TED Talks but with more stringent rules. An Ignite presentation must be 5 minutes long, accompanied by 20 slides that auto-advance every 15 seconds. The main ingredient for an effective Ignite presenter was his or her passion for the topic he was presenting on.

But the question arises: Why did CCIT decide to make this its first project? Being exposed to excruciating scientific presentations where the message is lost in mountains of text-heavy slides, Ignite's motto, "Enlighten us, but make it quick!" especially appealed to the organisers. It was an effort to promote lateral thinking in biomedicine, especially in a resource poor setting.

The presenters included doctors, researchers, students, creativity specialists and managers. All ten speakers presented on fields of expertise that had to be necessarily relevant to biomedicine and healthcare. The topics ranged from fashion to children's books to improvisational comedy to humour in medicine.

The event provided a platform to connect with a meaningful audience and definitely did ignite the younger crowd. Attended by people from all over AKU, and broadcast to AKU campuses abroad, the event proved to be a huge success. A new vision has been ignited at AKU.
